questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How people say sorry in different cultures
Why people find it hard to forgive
The history of the Ashanti kings
How to be polite on public transport
questions.why: They find out how apologies change from culture to culture.

questions.q: Why did Beth have to apologise that morning?
options: She was late for work
She criticised someone on TV
She stepped on someone's toes on the tube
She forgot her best friend's birthday party
questions.why: Beth says she stepped on someone's toes on the tube.

questions.q: Why does Neil compare Beth's apology with the story of Afia Pokua?
options: To show that both women were treated unfairly
To show that people in Ghana apologise much more than British people do
To explain that the word 'sorry' is always enough
To show that how you apologise depends on how serious the action was
questions.why: He says 'sorry' is fine for stepping on toes, but not for something really serious.

questions.q: What did the journalist Afia Pokua do?
options: She refused to meet the King
She criticised the King of the Ashanti tribe on television
She wrote a book about how people apologise in Ghana and Britain
She moved to the King's palace
questions.why: She made comments on television criticising the King of the Ashanti tribe.

questions.q: How did Afia apologise to the King?
options: She sent him a letter and a gift
She apologised on the same TV programme where she spoke
She followed tradition, wearing black and kneeling
She bowed and shook his hand
questions.why: She followed strict rules: to dress in black and apologise kneeling down.

questions.q: According to journalist Ahsan Mahmood, how do many Pakistanis apologise?
options: They slip it into a conversation and quickly change the subject
They apologise loudly and clearly in front of everyone who is there
They write a formal letter
They never apologise at all
questions.why: He says they slide an apology into a conversation and quickly move on to a new topic.

questions.q: What happens on Forgiveness Sunday in Russia, according to Liza Fokht?
options: People go to church and apologise to a priest for their bad actions
People call family and friends to say sorry for any sadness caused
Children apologise to their teachers
People give presents to their neighbours
questions.why: She says you call family and friends and apologise for any sorrows you've caused.

questions.q: What does Son Hun We say about saying sorry in Korea?
options: There is only one way to say it
People only apologise to their family
People avoid saying sorry to strangers because it's seen as a weakness
It depends on the relationship, and people often bow in formal cases
questions.why: He says it varies with the relationship, and people often bow when saying the formal phrase.
